safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 2.0 days

narrative: Material PL2__MC9F6B78 shows variable daily demand (CV=0.47) with a slight upward trend of +2.84 units/day over the observation window. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.58, range 0.34–5.20 days), contributing 74% of total lead-time-demand variance. The current SAP policy of zero safety stock is insufficient for the 95% service level target; a safety stock of 2,488 units is required. An (r,Q) policy is recommended with reorder point 4,730 and order quantity 6,890, constrained to 95.7% of available storage capacity.
warnings: Storage utilisation at 95.7% — limited headroom for demand spikes above 99th percentile
2 demand outliers winsorised at upper bound 3,326.5 units

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) — Continuous Review Reorder Point / Fixed Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is frequent (97.9% non-zero days) and variable (CV=0.47), making continuous review appropriate. EOQ provides cost-minimising order quantity well above MOQ (6,890 vs 2,274), and the reorder point with safety stock ensures 95% service level against combined demand and lead time uncertainty.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is 95.7% utilised post-replenishment (9,378 of 9,799 units). Any upward demand trend acceleration or supplier disruption causing larger emergency orders could breach capacity. Monitor rolling 30-day average demand and flag if it exceeds 1,350 units/day.
